title: Dynamic model stitching: latency vs cost playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook describing an experimental approach we call "dynamic model stitching" — switching between cheaper quantized model variants and higher-fidelity full models within the same session to reduce cost while protecting tail latency/SLOs. Goal is to capture operational heuristics, synthetic benchmark snapshots, and open questions for product/serving teams.

Summary of approach:
- Stitching idea: for a given conversation/session, use a small/quantized model (Q) for benign turns/prefixes and route to larger/original model (F) only when predicted quality or safety risk is high (triggered by intent classifier, perplexity delta, or explicit user signal).
- Expected win: lower amortized tokens-per-query cost for long sessions and for high-rate users while keeping p95/p99 latency when F is invoked.
- Failure modes: stitching adds routing latency, model warmup penalties, potential quality discontinuities mid-response.

Experimental setup (synthetic bench):
- Workload: mixed session mix with 60% short (<=2 turns), 30% medium (3-10 turns), 10% long (>10 turns). Turn length distribution: mean 24 tokens per turn.
- Models: F=base-Redwood-13B (full), Q=quant-Redwood-7B (INT4 experimental).
- Hardware: same GPU family (A100-like) with identical serving runtime kernel selection. Measured: cold/warm invocation latency, model switch overhead, per-token cost estimate (compute equivalent).
- Measurement units: 90s sustained and 30s spike windows. Cost normalized to compute-seconds per-1k-queries. Latency reported p50/p95/p99 in ms.

Key synthetic snapshots (text charts):
Scenario A: baseline (always F) vs stitching heuristic (Q until classifier confidence >0.7 then F).
- Cost per 1k queries (compute-seconds normalized):
  baseline: 1000 units
  stitching: 640 units (36% savings)
- Latency p95 / p99 (ms):
  baseline: p95=220, p99=360
  stitching (end-to-end observed): p95=240, p99=420
- Observations: stitching increases p99 due to warmups when F is invoked mid-turn, but p95 impact modest.

ASCII trend (cost vs p99 across trigger thresholds):
Trigger confidence threshold -> cost% of baseline | p99(ms)
  0.3 -> 48% | 520ms
  0.5 -> 58% | 470ms
  0.7 -> 64% | 420ms
  0.9 -> 82% | 370ms
(Interpretation: more aggressive switching to Q reduces cost but increases p99; there is a knee around 0.7 where cost savings still substantial and p99 remains somewhat controllable.)

Warmup and routing penalty breakdown (median per-switch):
- Routing decision time (classifier): 8ms
- KV cache transfer / context rebind: 45ms median, 120ms 95th
- Model activation (if cold): 600ms cold penalty (rare if prewarmed), 70ms warm hot-swap
- Total median switch penalty (warm path): ~125ms added latency to that turn

Micro-pattern cost accounting (example):
- Long session (15 turns, avg tokens/turn=20), baseline cost: 15*20*unit = 300 units; stitching with Q for first 10 turns + switch for final 5: Q-cost=10*20*0.18=36 units, switch overhead amortized=40 units, F-cost=5*20*1.0=100 => total 176 units vs 300 baseline = 41% cheaper.

Operational heuristics (early recommendations):
1) Prewarm strategy: maintain a small pool of F instances attached to active sessions with LRU eviction after N idle seconds. Tunable N recommended: 30-90s depending on session churn.
2) Soft fallback: when switching causes KV cache miss penalty > threshold, degrade to shorter partial responses rather than full re-run; rehydrate cache asynchronously.
3) Instrument per-tenant switch rates and p99 delta; alert if stitching causes >20% p99 regressions for more than 10 minutes.
4) Canary rollout: start stitching in dedicated A/B buckets with traffic caps (1-3%) and synthetic probes for worst-case sequences.

Quality regression sampling plan:
- Create a focused eval set of 200 sessions with known fidelity-sensitive prompts (e.g., multi-step math, code generation). Measure BLEU/ROUGE-like proxies and human pass/fail. Monitor stitch-induced hallucination rate increase.

Open questions / research items:
- Can prefix KV-cache be efficiently transferred between quantized and full variants without full re-encoding? (engineering spike)
- Is it possible to do incremental decoding with dual-model ensembles to hide switch latency (Q emits provisional tokens while F warms)? (architectural exploration)
- How to robustly signal to product when model quality discontinuity likely (UX signal)?

Limitations of this doc (known gaps):
- All benchmarks synthetic and use single GPU class; need multi-region/edge measurements.
- Cost normalized to compute-seconds, not actual billing; must map to committed reserved pricing and burst credits.
- Does not yet incorporate multi-modal requests or function-calling latency implications.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Platform: implement lightweight switch metrics (JIRA-PLAT-4823) and attach to tenant dashboards. (Diego)
- Serving runtime: prototype cache transfer spike (PR 712) and report cold/warm delta on real workloads. (Maya)
- Product/PD: assemble fidelity eval set and run human review on stitch vs baseline. (Liam)
- Ops: define canary rollout knobs and safe stop conditions.

Appendix: quick comparison table (human readable)
- Metric | baseline F-only | stitching (0.7 threshold)
  cost/1k | 1000 | 640
  p50 | 120ms | 130ms
  p95 | 220ms | 240ms
  p99 | 360ms | 420ms
  long-session cost reduction | baseline | ~40%
  short-session impact | none/minor | slight cost overhead due to classifier (~+5%)

Notes to reviewers: please add any real-world tenant ids we should include in the canary, and flag any regulatory/PII concerns with cache transfer. This is intentionally rough — meant as experimental playbook rather than a polished product spec.
